property_summary: For any caller, calls to fallback with exactly 10 ether always succeed (do not revert) on the reference C; the mutant requiring 5 ether will reject some inputs where the caller sends 10 ether and thus behave differently (revert vs succeed).

For any caller and any sent ETH amount, calls to C's payable fallback succeed iff the sent amount equals 10 ether; the reference always accepts exactly 10 ether while the mutant accepts 5 ether instead, so there exist fuzzed amounts (e.g. 10 ether) where the reference succeeds but the mutant rejects (or vice versa).

For every call to C.fallback with any sent ETH amount and any caller, the reference contract succeeds (does not revert) exactly when msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant instead requires msg.value == 5 ether, so there exist fuzzed msg.value and caller combinations where the reference accepts but the mutant reverts (or vice versa).

For any caller and any sent ether amount, the reference contract's payable fallback only accepts calls that send exactly 10 ether (non-reverting) and thus returns ok=true for those inputs; the mutant instead accepts exactly 5 ether, so there exist fuzzed amounts for which the reference returns ok=true but the mutant returns ok=false (or vice versa).

For every call to C's payable fallback, the correct contract accepts (does not revert) exactly when msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant instead accepts when msg.value == 5 ether, so fuzzing msg.value will find values that the reference accepts and the mutant rejects (and vice versa).

For any caller and any block.timestamp, when fallback is called with exactly 10 ether the reference contract always advances pastBlockTime to a strictly greater value than its previous value (i.e., pastBlockTime increases), whereas the mutant can allow a caller to set pastBlockTime to the same value across calls made within the same block time (because it removed the ordering require), violating monotonic increase across calls in same timestamp scenarios.

For any caller and any timestamp, calling fallback with exactly 10 ether on contract C either (1) reverts unless block.timestamp > pastBlockTime (reference) or (2) when it succeeds it always increases pastBlockTime to a value strictly greater than its previous value; the mutant (which removed the timestamp check) allows two consecutive successful calls in the same block timestamp to leave pastBlockTime unchanged across the two calls, violating monotonic increase across successful calls made at equal block.timestamp.

For any caller and any timestamp, whenever fallback is invoked with exactly 10 ether and the call succeeds, the reference contract ensures pastBlockTime strictly increases (is set to block.timestamp+1 which must be > previous pastBlockTime due to the require), whereas the mutant (which removed the require) can allow two successful fallback calls in the same block timestamp to produce a non-increasing pastBlockTime, so the universal rule is: after a successful fallback call pastBlockTime > oldPastBlockTime; the mutant can violate this for some inputs.

For every successful payable fallback call with exactly 10 ether, C always sets pastBlockTime to a strictly greater value than it had before the call (pastBlockTime increases); the mutant that removed the timestamp require allows a successful call that does not increase pastBlockTime for some inputs (two calls in the same block timestamp), violating this rule.

For any successful payable fallback call with exactly 10 ether, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to a value strictly greater than its previous value; the mutant (which removed the require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime)) allows a successful call that does not increase pastBlockTime for some inputs (two successful calls in the same block timestamp), breaking this rule.

For any caller and any block timestamp/number, after a successful fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether and satisfies the time check, the stored pastBlockTime in the reference is always equal to block.timestamp + 1 (so <= block.timestamp + 10) while the mutant sets it to block.timestamp + 10, so there exist inputs (timestamps) where the mutant's pastBlockTime differs — we assert the reference's getter equals block.timestamp + 1 after the call.

After any successful payable fallback call that accepts exactly 10 ether and when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to block.timestamp + 1; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp + 10, so there exist inputs where the stored pastBlockTime differs (the property: c.pastBlockTime() == block.timestamp + 1 after the call).

For any caller and timestamp/amount inputs that satisfy the contract's requirements, calling C.fallback with exactly 10 ether never empties the contract balance immediately unless the block number is a multiple of 15; the mutant always empties the balance, violating this conditional-transfer rule for some inputs.

For every admissible call that sends exactly 10 ether and advances time, the reference contract only empties its balance and returns funds to the caller when block.number % 15 == 0, whereas the mutant always transfers the balance, so the general rule is: after a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, address(c).balance == 0 iff block.number % 15 == 0; the mutant violates this by making balance 0 for some inputs where block.number % 15 != 0.

For every fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether and advances time (block.timestamp > pastBlockTime), the reference contract only empties its balance when block.number is a multiple of 15; the mutant empties it when block.number is NOT a multiple of 15, so the property is that address(c).balance == 0 iff block.number % 15 == 0 (reference) which the mutant violates for some block numbers.

For any call that sends exactly 10 ether and occurs at a strictly greater timestamp than the previous call, the reference contract empties its balance (address(c).balance == 0) if and only if the current block.number is a multiple of 15; the mutant inverts that condition and therefore will misalign which block numbers result in balance == 0 for some fuzzed block numbers.

For any caller and any block timestamp strictly greater than the stored pastBlockTime, invoking fallback with exactly 10 ether advances pastBlockTime to a value strictly greater than the pre-call pastBlockTime (i.e., it sets pastBlockTime > old pastBlockTime); the mutant that sets pastBlockTime = block.timestamp (instead of block.timestamp + 1) can leave pastBlockTime equal to block.timestamp and thereby can make the stored value not strictly greater than the previous value for some inputs.

For any call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to a value that is strictly greater than block.timestamp - i.e., pastBlockTime >= block.timestamp + 1 after the call; the mutant can set pastBlockTime == block.timestamp, violating that invariant for some inputs.

For any call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the correct contract always sets pastBlockTime to a strictly larger value than the previous pastBlockTime (specifically pastBlockTime becomes block.timestamp + 1), whereas the mutant can set it to block.timestamp, which for some inputs does not increase pastBlockTime and thus violates the monotonic increase property.

For any successful payable fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to a value strictly greater than block.timestamp (block.timestamp + 1), whereas the mutant may set pastBlockTime == block.timestamp, violating that inequality for some inputs.

For any successful payable fallback call (msg.value == 10 ether) when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference contract always sets pastBlockTime to a value that is strictly greater than the value read immediately after the call (i.e., address(c).pastBlockTime() > block.timestamp), while the mutant can leave pastBlockTime equal to block.timestamp causing address(c).pastBlockTime() <= block.timestamp for some inputs.
